title: Digit workshop: Boss receipt
summary: For each reading, produce the sum of the decimal digits of its absolute value; the digit sum of 0 is 0. Return the weighted sum of the derived sequence: multiply its first value by 1, its second by 2, and so on, then add the products. Return 0 for an empty sequence.
revisit: Earlier foundation work; the first unit establishes the prerequisite
descriptionMd:
Loose digit wheels from an old numbering machine need a handwritten inspection ledger. Rafi adds numbered weights to the final receipt at the unit's inspection desk. The first derived reading has weight one, so its position matters as much as its value.

For each reading, produce the sum of the decimal digits of its absolute value; the digit sum of 0 is 0.

Return the weighted sum of the derived sequence: multiply its first value by 1, its second by 2, and so on, then add the products. Return 0 for an empty sequence.

Implement digitWorkshopBossReceipt(readings, k). k is part of the common inspection-card signature and does not affect this task's result.
unitIntro: Helper functions. For each reading, produce the sum of the decimal digits of its absolute value; the digit sum of 0 is 0. Keep the sequence order specified here before computing the requested receipt. A scan invariant says what has been processed and what remains. Work through the proof strip first, then change the returned summary without changing the definition of that sequence. The last card revisits loop accumulators from Hello, Keys (earlier units are used while the first two levels establish the foundations).
constraints: 1 <= k <= 8. All arithmetic results fit a signed 32-bit integer.
Numeric readings lie between -1,000,000 and 1,000,000, subject to the task's shape and ordering rules.

Target time O(n); auxiliary space including the derived sequence O(n). n is the input length; d distinct values; q query count; M maximum reading; V vertices; E edges; h tree height; r reported tree nodes.
hints: Start with helper functions. What state describes the portion you have already processed?

For each reading, produce the sum of the decimal digits of its absolute value; the digit sum of 0 is 0. Derive each required reading once; do not restart the whole procedure for every output position.

Return the weighted sum of the derived sequence: multiply its first value by 1, its second by 2, and so on, then add the products. Return 0 for an empty sequence. Use an accumulator and a one-based position counter, revisiting the first level's loop work.

cases.explanation: The derived sequence is [7,3,7,0,3]. Its weighted products are [7,6,21,0,15]. Return the weighted sum of the derived sequence: multiply its first value by 1, its second by 2, and so on, then add the products. Return 0 for an empty sequence. This gives 49.

The derived sequence is [4,4,2,4]. Its weighted products are [4,8,6,16]. Return the weighted sum of the derived sequence: multiply its first value by 1, its second by 2, and so on, then add the products. Return 0 for an empty sequence. This gives 34.
